question.text: Will the most viewed English Wikipedia article during the week of December 20-26, 2026 be an individual human?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as Yes if the highest viewed English Wikipedia article during the week of December 20th to December 26 is an individual human. The primary source for this question will be [Top 25 Report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Top_25_Report). If it is not available or found to be inaccurate, another source may be used.
question.fine_print:
To qualify the article must be titled as some form of their name, including aliases. 
Articles about an event involving a person, such as "Death of X" will not count. 
Fictional characters will not count. 
The article title may include a disambiguation such as "Name (Occupation)". 
If it is unknown whether an article refers to an individual person, such as an anonymous entity, this question will assume it does not count.

research:

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-15: The current [Top 25 Report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Top_25_Report) covers Nov 1-7, 2026. #1 was **Abdul El-Sayed** (3,687,537 views), a person, likely tied to the US midterms. Next were 2026 United States elections (2.64M), Ramayana: Part 1 (2.42M) and James Talarico (2.13M). Report weeks run Sunday to Saturday, and Dec 20-26, 2026 (Sunday to Saturday) is exactly one report week.
- The [Number-one articles list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Top_25_Report/Number-one_articles) was too long to read in full. I got entries through mid-2024 and checked the 2024 and 2025 Christmas weeks on the individual report pages.

- Nothing settles the question yet. The week is five weeks away.

Across all weeks of the year, people are #1 roughly 40-50% of the time, judging from the 2024 entries I read.

(b) If nothing unexpected happens, Avengers: Doomsday (and possibly Dune: Part Three), both opening Dec 18, will hold #1 in their first full week. That resolves No.

(c) Base rate: a person was #1 in about 2 of the last 13 comparable Christmas weeks, roughly 15%. In years with a mega-franchise opening the weekend before Christmas (Star Wars in 2015, 2017 and 2019, Spider-Man in 2021), the rate was 0 of 4.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - People are #1 in about 40-50% of ordinary weeks, for example Abdul El-Sayed in Nov 1-7, 2026.
  - A person came close in recent Christmas weeks: Manmohan Singh was #2, about 0.25M behind, in 2024, and James Ransone was #3 in 2025.
  - Celebrity deaths have given person #1s nearby: Zsa Zsa Gabor in 2016, Carrie Fisher in 2016, Andrew Tate in 2022.
- **For No:**
  - Avengers: Doomsday presales are over $70M domestic (Nov 2026) and opening tracking runs to $260-450M, so its article will likely draw 3.5-5M+ views. Spider-Man: No Way Home drew 3.73M in the same week of 2021.
  - Dune: Part Three adds a second strong film competitor.
  - Christmas, Boxing Day, Indian films and Netflix releases also compete.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** Avengers: Doomsday has a record opening and its article gets around 4-5M views in Dec 20-26, comfortably ahead of everything else.
- **Yes:** A globally beloved celebrity or major political figure dies or is arrested around Dec 20-22. Their article passes 5M views and edges out the film.

(f) I start at 15%. I move down because a record-scale blockbuster opens two days before the week, a pattern that produced a film #1 every time it occurred. A person beating a ~4M+ film requires a top-tier death or news shock in a narrow window. I nudge slightly back up because such shocks are unpredictable and person articles have recently landed close to #1. My final estimate is about 10%.
